note: The original gives the measurements with a comma as the decimal separator (for example 1,25 mm), converted here to a point with the values unchanged. The alate is unknown. Type locality data: 24 km from Kitwe through the Mwekera Forest Reserve, Zambia, collected on 1957-1-23 by W. G. H. Coaton.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Related to P. hirticeps and P. minutus; the mean soldier measurements fall between the two and overlap extensively, but in this species the mesonotum and metanotum are wider, the difference between metanotum width and pronotum width being about 0.1 mm in every specimen, whereas in the other two it is only about 0.05 mm. P. prorepens and P. minimus are distinctly smaller in body size and can be separated from this species by size alone. The head capsule of this species is smoky-tinted, a shade apparently absent in P. hirticeps and P. minutus. When disturbed the soldier secretes a large amount of white sticky oral fluid, so that specimens in a vial set into a gelatinous mass; this is a feature shared by the genus. The nest consists of a low earth mound with 6 chimney-like structures up to 28 cm high, each chimney containing a vertical ventilation shaft; some chimneys are completely closed, while in others the shaft opens at the summit through a lateral opening.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head capsule pale smoky brown; mandibles dark reddish brown to black at the apex, the basal third smoky brown; postmentum concolorous with the ventral genae. Thoracic and abdominal tergites smoky yellow; intersegmental membranes nearly white. Legs concolorous with the thoracic tergites, the tibiae paler than the femora. Head capsule broadly rectangular in dorsal view, the sides straight to slightly convex, the fontanelle invisible; in lateral view the upper and lower surfaces slightly and evenly convex, the postmentum convex and projecting. Mandibles curved upward, fine at the apex; the outer margin of the right mandible evenly convex, that of the left mandible with a slight swelling at the level of the second marginal tooth. Postmentum distinctly narrowed towards the anterior end in dorsal view. Antenna 15 segments, segment 1 the longest, segment 3 the shortest, segments 4—6 about as long as wide, segments 7—15 oval and gradually larger towards the apex. Head capsule with evident but not dense hairs. Anterior end of the labrum in a pointed arch, without a translucent tip. Pronotum half the width of the head capsule, saddle-shaped, notched on both the anterior and the posterior margin; metanotum distinctly wider than the pronotum.

Soldier measurements (holotype; range/mean for 67 individuals, mm): head length (to the outer mandibular base) 1.25/1.20—1.33/1.27; greatest head width 1.03/1.00—1.08/1.04; head depth (including the postmentum) 0.79/0.76—0.83/0.79; postmentum length 0.83/0.80—0.86/0.84; greatest postmentum width 0.54/0.51—0.56/0.54; least postmentum width 0.48/0.45—0.50/0.49; left mandible length 0.65/0.60—0.68/0.65; hind tibia length 1.05/0.99—1.08/1.05; greatest pronotum length 0.52/0.50—0.55/0.52; pronotum width 0.82/0.79—0.86/0.83; mesonotum width 0.80/0.78—0.85/0.81; metanotum width 0.91/0.90—1.00/0.94.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Large worker: head capsule reddish yellow, with denser hairs than in the soldier; in dorsal view the sides are straighter behind the outer mandibular articulation. Postclypeus more than 2 times as wide as long, distinctly inflated, the posterior margin convex, the anterior margin concave. Antenna 17 segments. Head width 1.31—1.35 mm in 10 individuals, mean 1.32 mm.

Small worker: head capsule smoky yellow. Postclypeus more inflated than in the large worker, more than 2 times as wide as long, the posterior margin convex, the anterior margin straight. Antenna 15 segments. Head width 0.93—0.96 mm in 5 individuals, mean 0.94 mm.
